item.title: Trial of former FBC CEO and executive to begin after adjournment bid dismissed
item.description: The trial of former Fiji Broadcasting Corporation chief executive officer Riyaz Sayed-Khaiyum and chief financial officer Vimlesh Sagar formally begins tomorrow after the Suva Magistrate’s Court dismissed prosecution application for an adjournment. Magistrate Charles Ratakele ruled that FICAC’s application did not establish good cause, noting that the matter is almost two and a half years old.
item.content:encoded:
The trial of former Fiji Broadcasting Corporation chief executive officer Riyaz Sayed-Khaiyum and chief financial officer Vimlesh Sagar formally begins tomorrow after the Suva Magistrate’s Court dismissed prosecution application for an adjournment.

Magistrate Charles Ratakele ruled that FICAC’s application did not establish good cause, noting that the matter is almost two and a half years old.

Mr Sayed-Khaiyum faces charges of abuse of office for gain and an alternative charge of general dishonesty causing a loss, while Mr Sagar is charged with general dishonesty.

Mr Sayed-Khaiyum is alleged to have pursued five legal proceedings without the knowledge and approval of the FBC board of directors at a cost of $138,813.37, which were not in the interest of the company.

The alleged incidents occurred between July 1, 2017, and January 31, 2023.

Mr Sagar is charged with general dishonesty, having allegedly caused a loss by approving payments to R. Patel Lawyers without the prior approval of the FBC board, amounting to $15,075.88.

Senior FICAC prosecutor Setefano Komaibaba made the application, telling the court that two prosecution witnesses considered crucial to the case were currently unavailable.

The prosecution submitted that efforts were being made to secure the witnesses and argued that their absence provided grounds for the trial to be adjourned.

The defence opposed the application, arguing that the matter was more than two years old and that both accused were ready to proceed with the trial.

The defence submitted that the prosecution had to provide sufficient evidence explaining why the witnesses were unavailable, what steps had been taken to secure their attendance and whether there was a reasonable assurance they would be available at a later date.

It also argued that the accused had constitutional rights to have the matter determined within a reasonable time and should not bear the consequences of delays attributable to the prosecution.

The defence further highlighted the financial and personal impact of repeated trial delays, noting that the accused had been preparing for the trial since the charges were filed in 2024.

The prosecution maintained that the witnesses were important to its case and that it was seeking time to secure their attendance.

In a public notice, the RFMF said the exercise will involve blank ammunition, pyrotechnics and heavy explosive sounds designed to simulate battle
item.content:encoded:
RESIDENTS and visitors around Vuda Marina and Serenity Island are being warned to expect military vessels, personnel, water police movements and loud simulated explosions today as the Republic of Fiji Military Forces conducts Exercise Bougainville 2026.

In a public notice, the RFMF said the exercise will involve blank ammunition, pyrotechnics and heavy explosive sounds designed to simulate battle conditions.

The RFMF has urged the public not to be alarmed by the activity but to exercise caution while travelling through the affected areas.

It said safety measures were in place to minimise risks and ensure the exercise was conducted safely and professionally.

item.title: Families displaced after Nausori fire
item.description: THREE families have been displaced after a fire destroyed a three-flat home at Hooker Subdivision in Nausori yesterday. Flat owner Yogeshni Singh, who lives a few houses away from the property, said she received a call from one of the tenants at around 1pm informing her that the house was on fire.
item.content:encoded:
THREE families have been displaced after a fire destroyed a three-flat home at Hooker Subdivision in Nausori yesterday.

Flat owner Yogeshni Singh, who lives a few houses away from the property, said she received a call from one of the tenants at around 1pm informing her that the house was on fire.

Ms Singh said she rushed to the scene, but by the time she arrived, the fire had already engulfed the entire building.

“It was too late by the time we got here,” she said.

She said strong winds caused the fire to spread quickly through the three flats leaving the families without a home.

Ms Singh confirmed that there were no fatalities.

She said the fire was believed to have started in the middle flat, although the family living there had already left the property by the time she arrived.

Police officers at the scene also confirmed that no serious injuries had been reported.

The cause of the fire remains undetermined as investigations continue.

item.title: UN drives regional revival of Pacific cooperatives in Fiji
item.description: PACIFIC Island nations must harness the power of community-driven development to combat pressing economic and environmental challenges,says UN Social Affairs Officer Andrew Allimadi. Speaking yesterday at the opening of the Strengthening Pacific Cooperatives workshop at the Tanoa International Hotel in Nadi yesterday,Mr Allimadi urged regional leaders to rebuild cooperative traditions.
item.content:encoded:
PACIFIC Island nations must harness the power of community-driven development to combat pressing economic and environmental challenges,says UN Social Affairs Officer Andrew Allimadi.

Speaking yesterday at the opening of the Strengthening Pacific Cooperatives workshop at the Tanoa International Hotel in Nadi yesterday,Mr Allimadi urged regional leaders to rebuild cooperative traditions.

“I think it is very fitting that we are in Fiji today, a country that has recognised the power of collective action and community-driven development,” he said.

“Over the next three days, we will focus on a simple but powerful idea: when people work together, they can achieve far more than they can do so alone.”

Mr Allimadi said that local development remains urgent across the Pacific, where isolated communities continue to confront geographic barriers, climate change, and youth unemployment.

“World leaders gathered in Doha for the Second World Summit for Social Development and reaffirmed a fundamental truth: development is ultimately about people.

“One way to solve a lot of these problems is to bring back the power of cooperatives.”

Mr Allimadi highlighted that major global summits, including the Sustainable Development Goals initiatives, have consistently acknowledged cooperative models as vital engines for sustainable local progress.

“The Pacific has a proud cooperative tradition. The opportunity before us is to build a legacy by strengthening the skills, institutions, and enabling environment.

“We need strong political will and strong political leadership to drive this system forward.”

item.title: Mobile wallet scoops major regional award, dedicates win to customers
item.description: Digital Financial Services Pte Limited’s (DFS) M-PAiSA mobile wallet platform won the PayTech of the Year Award category at the Asia FinTech Awards 2026 in Singapore over the weekend. The award recognises excellence, innovation, and impact among the region’s leading financial technology providers.
item.content:encoded:
Digital Financial Services Pte Limited’s (DFS) M-PAiSA mobile wallet platform won the PayTech of the Year Award category at the Asia FinTech Awards 2026 in Singapore over the weekend.

The award recognises excellence, innovation, and impact among the region’s leading financial technology providers.

DFS general manager Shailendra Prasad said to be recognised among Asia’s fintech industry stalwarts was a tremendous honour.

He said as a company from a small Pacific island nation, the award demonstrated that innovation was not defined by the size of the market, but rather by the impact it has on people’s lives.

Mr Prasad acknowledged and dedicated the award to their M-PAISA customers.

He acknowledged the teams, business partners, merchants, agents and technology providers for their patronage and believing in the vision of a platform that now served hundreds of thousands of Fijians every day.

He also acknowledged the Reserve Bank of Fiji (RBF) and the wider regulatory community.

“Progressive regulation and collaboration have played a critical role in enabling innovation while maintaining trust and security within the financial system,” Mr Prasad said in his acceptance remark.

“Over the years, we have remained committed to innovation and to pushing the boundaries of what is possible.

“We persevered, we tried and we tried until we got it right.”

Mr Prasad said what made them most proud was not the technology itself but the impact.

“It is the rural farmer or the fisherman across the seas who can accept digital payments instantly without needing a traditional banking relationship. It is the woman entrepreneur who now has greater control over her finances to grow her business. It is the family member overseas who can send money home to loved ones in seconds from over 94 countries.”

He said the was the true meaning of financial inclusion.

“As we celebrate tonight, we recognise that this award is not the destination. It is a reminder that innovation must continue.

“There are still communities to serve, barriers to remove and opportunities to create.

“We remain committed to building solutions that empower people, strengthen businesses, promote inclusion, and contribute to economic growth across Fiji and the Pacific.”

item.title: Man gets 15 years for raping niece, 16
item.description: A 29-YEAR-OLD married man has been sentenced to 15 years in prison for raping his 16-year-old niece on two consecutive days. Justice Lee James Burney sentenced the man at the High Court in Labasa on August 14 after he was convicted following a trial.
item.content:encoded:
A 29-YEAR-OLD married man has been sentenced to 15 years in prison for raping his 16-year-old niece on two consecutive days.

Justice Lee James Burney sentenced the man at the High Court in Labasa on August 14 after he was convicted following a trial.

The man was convicted of two counts of rape relating to offences committed on October 4 and 5, 2025.

The court was told the victim was living with her aunt, uncle, and other family members when the man came to stay with them during the cane-cutting season.

On October 4, the victim was awoken by him touching her leg. When she returned from the washroom, he stood in front of her before raping her.

The following day, he followed her into the washroom and raped her again.

The court heard the victim continued to suffer fear, nightmares, and embarrassment, had difficulty trusting male relatives and struggled to concentrate on her studies.

The man must serve nine years and two months of his head sentence before being eligible for parole.

item.title: Needle sharing warning
item.description: FIJI’S health authorities are raising concern over injecting drug users sharing needles, with some reportedly using the same needle for almost 90 days. Ministry of Health principal medical officer Dr Sailosi Soqo warned that without stronger intervention, the number of HIV cases could reach 25,000 within the next three to four years.
item.content:encoded:
FIJI’S health authorities are raising concern over injecting drug users sharing needles, with some reportedly using the same needle for almost 90 days.

Ministry of Health principal medical officer Dr Sailosi Soqo warned that without stronger intervention, the number of HIV cases could reach 25,000 within the next three to four years.

“If we don’t do anything in the next three to four years, we’ll be reaching 25,000 cases,” he said.

Speaking at the 43rd Fiji Head Teachers Association annual conference in Nadi, Dr Soqo said Government was strengthening its response through greater coordination, new prevention measures and increased resources.

He said a specialised unit had been established under Dr Jason Mitchell, with different leads overseeing key areas.

The national counter-narcotic strategy involves multiple agencies, with the Ministry of Education leading demand reduction, health responsible for harm reduction and police handling supply reduction.

Dr Soqo said Government was recruiting more personnel and receiving donor funding to strengthen programs.

He highlighted the Needle and Syringe Program, designed to reduce risks from needle sharing, as well as pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP), which helps prevent HIV infection.

“We have the medication. Our strategies are there, but people are not coming forward.”

item.title: More than 723,000 voters registered
item.description: Fiji had 723,771 registered voters as of June 30, 2026, with the Central Division accounting for the largest share of the country’s electorate. The latest 2026 National Register of Voters Statistics show the Central Division has 313,135 registered voters, followed by the Western Division with 270,175.
item.content:encoded:
Fiji had 723,771 registered voters as of June 30, 2026, with the Central Division accounting for the largest share of the country’s electorate.

The latest 2026 National Register of Voters Statistics show the Central Division has 313,135 registered voters, followed by the Western Division with 270,175.

The Northern Division recorded 102,304 voters, while the Eastern Division had 25,266.

A further 12,891 voters were registered overseas.

The statistics also show an almost even gender split among registered voters, with 362,438 males and 361,333 females — a difference of just 1,105 voters.

Among male voters, the largest age group is 21 to 30 years, with 73,724 registered voters, followed by those aged 31 to 40 with 64,376.

For females, the 21 to 30 age category is also the largest, accounting for 73,226 voters, while 60,052 are aged between 31 and 40.

The figures show younger voters make up a significant portion of Fiji’s electoral roll, with more than 146,000 men and women registered in the 21-to-30 age bracket.

At the other end of the age spectrum, 15,722 male voters and 8,819 female voters are aged 81 years and above.

The voter statistics provide a snapshot of Fiji’s electorate as preparations continue towards the country’s next general election.

The figures are based on the National Register of Voters as at June 30, 2026.
